title: Three-Phase Power
summary: Wye and delta systems, why line and phase values differ by the square root of three, how 208Y/120 V and 480Y/277 V buildings are put together, and how to calculate three-phase current, power and neutral current.
objectives: Students will be able to explain what makes a system three-phase and why it is used for motors and large buildings.
Students will be able to distinguish wye from delta connections and state the line-to-phase relationships for voltage and current in each.
Students will be able to calculate load current and power for three-phase loads using the √3 formulas, and compute neutral current for an unbalanced wye.
Students will be able to describe 208Y/120 V, 480Y/277 V and 240/120 V high-leg delta systems and identify the high leg correctly.
Students will be able to explain phase rotation and how reversing it affects a three-phase motor.

sections.heading: What three-phase means
sections.markdown:
A single-phase supply is one alternating voltage. A **three-phase** supply is three alternating voltages of equal magnitude, generated by three windings spaced around the same generator, so each one reaches its peak one-third of a cycle (120°) after the previous one. The three windings share a common return, which lets three conductors do the work that would otherwise take six.

Why the industry bothers:

- **More power per pound of copper.** Three conductors carry √3 (about 1.73) times the power of a two-conductor single-phase line at the same line current and voltage, for only 1.5 times the conductor material.
- **Smooth power.** Single-phase power pulses to zero 120 times a second; the sum of three phases is constant, which is why three-phase motors run smoother and vibrate less.
- **Self-starting motors.** Three phases produce a rotating magnetic field automatically. Single-phase motors need start windings, capacitors or shaded poles to get going.
- **Smaller motors and transformers** for the same horsepower.

Residential service in the United States is single-phase 120/240 V. Nearly every commercial, industrial and institutional building is three-phase, and electricians who understand the two connection types, **wye** and **delta**, can read any one-line diagram.

sections.title: Three voltages, 120° apart
sections.caption: Phase A (gold), phase B (blue) and phase C (green). At any instant the three add to zero, which is why a balanced wye system carries no neutral current and why a delta needs no neutral at all.

sections.caption: In a wye the three windings share a center point, which becomes the neutral. In a delta the windings form a closed loop. The terminal letters A, B, C match the line conductors; the neutral of a wye is marked X0 on a transformer.

sections.name: Line vs phase relationships
sections.expression: Wye:  V_line = √3 × V_phase,  I_line = I_phase        Delta:  V_line = V_phase,  I_line = √3 × I_phase

variables.meaning: voltage between any two line conductors (A–B, B–C, C–A)
voltage across one winding (line-to-neutral in a wye)
current in one winding or one leg of a delta-connected load

sections.explanation: The √3 comes from adding two sine waves that are 120° apart. In a wye, the line conductor is the winding, so the currents are equal but the line-to-line voltage is the vector sum of two windings: 120 V × 1.732 = 208 V. In a delta, the line-to-line voltage is one winding, but each line conductor carries current from two windings: I_line = 1.732 × I_phase.

sections.name: Three-phase power
sections.expression: P = √3 × V_line × I_line × PF        S = √3 × V_line × I_line

variables.meaning: power factor of the load (1.0 for heaters, 0.8–0.9 for motors)

sections.explanation: These formulas use line values and work for wye or delta loads alike, as long as the load is balanced. Rearranged, I_line = S ÷ (√3 × V_line) is the formula you use for sizing conductors and breakers for three-phase equipment rated in kVA or kW.

sections.problem: A 480 V, three-phase electric heater is rated 30 kW (resistive, PF = 1.0). Find the line current. Then find the line current of a 480 V three-phase motor that draws 25 kW at 0.85 power factor.
solutionSteps: Notice the motor draws almost the same current for less real power: the lower power factor means more apparent power (S = 29.4 kVA) for 25 kW of work.
For NEC conductor sizing, a motor uses the Table 430.250 full-load current rather than this calculated value; the calculation is still the right way to understand what the nameplate numbers mean.
sections.answer: Heater 36.1 A; motor 35.4 A per line conductor.

sections.heading: The high-leg delta: a trap for the unwary
sections.markdown:
Some older buildings are served from a 240 V delta transformer bank in which one winding is center-tapped and grounded to provide 120 V. Two phases (A and C) measure 120 V to neutral, but the third phase, B, sits at the far corner of the triangle and measures **208 V to neutral** (120 × √3). That phase is the **high leg** (also called the wild leg or stinger).

Rules and habits that keep this from burning up equipment:

- The high leg must be durably marked **orange** (or by another effective means) wherever a connection is made and the neutral is also present (NEC 110.15).
- In a panelboard or switchboard the high leg goes on **phase B**, the center bus (408.3(E)), with a specific exception for metering equipment where the utility may require it elsewhere.
- Never put a 120 V single-pole breaker on the B phase of a high-leg panel. Measure every phase to neutral before adding a circuit to an unfamiliar panel.
- Three-pole loads (motors) see 240 V between all three phases and do not care about the high leg; only line-to-neutral loads are affected.

sections.text: Reading 208 V between one phase and neutral in a panel that otherwise shows 120 V is the signature of a high-leg delta. Stop and confirm the system type before connecting anything line-to-neutral. Conversely, reading 120 V on all three phases to neutral and 208 V phase-to-phase tells you it is a 208Y/120 wye, where every phase is safe for 120 V loads.

sections.heading: Neutral current and unbalance
sections.markdown:
In a four-wire wye, the neutral carries the vector sum of the three line currents. For balanced resistive loads the sum is zero, which is why the neutral is permitted to be smaller than the phase conductors in some cases (220.61). When the loads are unbalanced the neutral carries the difference, and the worst single-phase case (one phase loaded, two phases off) puts the full load current on the neutral.

For resistive (unity power factor) loads the neutral current is:

I_N = √(Ia² + Ib² + Ic² − Ia·Ib − Ib·Ic − Ic·Ia)

Electronic loads (computers, LED drivers, VFDs) draw **third-harmonic** currents (180 Hz) that do **not** cancel in the neutral; they add. A neutral serving mostly electronic loads can carry more current than any phase conductor. This is why 310.15(E) counts a neutral that serves major nonlinear loads as a current-carrying conductor, why K-rated transformers exist, and why you should clamp the neutral whenever you survey a panel full of office equipment.

sections.problem: A 208Y/120 V panel supplies resistive loads of 40 A on phase A, 25 A on phase B and 10 A on phase C. Find the neutral current. What would it be if the loads were balanced at 40 A each?
sections.answer: Neutral current is 26.0 A unbalanced and 0 A balanced. Balancing loads across phases is not just neatness; it reduces neutral current, voltage drop and transformer heating.

sections.heading: Phase rotation, identification and testing
sections.markdown:
**Rotation (sequence).** The order in which the phases peak, ABC or CBA, is the phase rotation. A three-phase motor turns in the direction set by the rotation of its supply; swapping any two line leads reverses it. A pump run backwards moves little water, a compressor run backwards can destroy itself in minutes, and an elevator run backwards is dangerous. Check rotation with a **phase rotation meter** before connecting critical equipment, and bump-test motors (a momentary start) to confirm direction before coupling them to the load.

**Identification.** The NEC does not assign colors to ungrounded phase conductors, except that the high leg is orange and the grounded conductor is white or gray. Common California practice is black-red-blue for 208Y/120 and brown-orange-yellow for 480Y/277. Where a building has more than one nominal voltage system, 210.5(C) requires each ungrounded conductor to be identified by phase and system at every termination and the scheme posted at each panel.

**Testing a new three-phase feed.** Before load is connected, measure A–B, B–C, C–A and A–N, B–N, C–N. All three line-to-line values should agree within about 1 %. **Voltage unbalance** above 1–2 % causes current unbalance in motors of six to ten times that percentage, overheating the windings; NEMA MG 1 recommends derating motors above 1 % unbalance. A missing phase (single-phasing) shows as one line-to-line reading near zero or far off and will burn out a running motor unless the overloads trip.

**Numbers to memorize.** Keep 1.732 and 0.577 (its reciprocal) in your head. Line-to-neutral on a wye is line-to-line × 0.577 (480 × 0.577 = 277; 208 × 0.577 = 120). Three-phase current from kVA is kVA × 1000 ÷ (1.732 × V), which works out to 2.78 A per kVA at 208 V and 1.20 A per kVA at 480 V; with those two figures you can size most three-phase loads in your head.

practice.prompt: A wye-connected transformer secondary provides 277 V line-to-neutral. What is the line-to-line voltage?
A 208 V three-phase load is rated 15 kVA. What line current does it draw?
A delta-connected load has 20 A flowing in each winding (phase current). What is the line current?
practice.explanation: In a delta, I_line = √3 × I_phase = 1.732 × 20 = 34.6 A.

practice.prompt: A 480 V three-phase motor draws 52 A at a power factor of 0.88. How much real power does it consume, in kW?
practice.explanation: P = 1.732 × 480 × 52 × 0.88 = 38,044 W = 38.0 kW (38.1 with unrounded intermediate values).

practice.prompt: In a 240/120 V high-leg delta system, the conductor that reads 208 V to neutral must be:
choices: identified orange and landed on phase B in the panelboard
identified white and used as the neutral
identified green and bonded to the enclosure
removed, because 208 V is not a legal voltage
practice.explanation: NEC 110.15 requires orange (or another effective) identification of the high leg, and 408.3(E) puts it on phase B. It carries 208 V to neutral because of the √3 relationship.

practice.prompt: A three-phase pump motor runs backwards after installation. The correct fix is to:
choices: swap any two of the three line leads at the motor or starter
swap all three line leads
reverse the neutral connection
install a larger overload relay
practice.explanation: Swapping two leads reverses phase rotation and therefore the direction of the rotating field. Swapping all three leaves the rotation unchanged.

practice.prompt: A 208Y/120 V panel has resistive loads of 30 A, 30 A and 0 A on phases A, B and C. What current flows in the neutral?
practice.explanation: I_N = √(900 + 900 + 0 − 900 − 0 − 0) = √900 = 30 A. Two equal phases 120° apart leave a neutral current equal to one phase current.

questions.prompt: A 208Y/120 V system: what voltage is measured between any one phase and the neutral?
questions.explanation: Line-to-neutral in a wye is line-to-line ÷ 1.732 = 208 ÷ 1.732 = 120 V.

questions.prompt: A three-phase 480 V load draws 100 A per line at a power factor of 1.0. What is its power in kW?
A 75 kVA three-phase transformer has a 480 V secondary. What is its rated secondary line current?
The three voltages of a three-phase system are separated in time by:
choices: 90 electrical degrees
120 electrical degrees
180 electrical degrees
60 electrical degrees
questions.explanation: Three equal phases are spaced evenly through a 360° cycle: 360 ÷ 3 = 120°.

questions.prompt: In a wye-connected system, which statement is true?
choices: Line current equals phase current, and line voltage is √3 times phase voltage
Line voltage equals phase voltage, and line current is √3 times phase current
Line and phase values are always equal
There is never a neutral conductor
questions.explanation: In a wye the line conductor is in series with its winding (same current), while line-to-line voltage spans two windings (√3 × phase). The delta relationship is the reverse.

questions.prompt: Why can the neutral in a panel full of computers and LED drivers carry more current than any phase conductor?
choices: Because the neutral is always undersized
Because third-harmonic currents from electronic loads add in the neutral instead of cancelling
Because the loads are perfectly balanced
Because the neutral carries the √3 factor
questions.explanation: Triplen harmonics (180 Hz and multiples) are in phase on all three lines and sum in the neutral. Balanced fundamental currents cancel; harmonics do not.

questions.prompt: You measure 480 V between all phase pairs and 277 V from each phase to neutral. The system is:
choices: a 480Y/277 V wye
a 480 V corner-grounded delta
a 240/120 V high-leg delta
a 208Y/120 V wye
questions.explanation: 480 ÷ 1.732 = 277 V line-to-neutral on every phase identifies a 480Y/277 V wye.

questions.prompt: Before coupling a new three-phase motor to a compressor, the best practice is to:
choices: run it coupled and reverse it if the compressor sounds wrong
check phase rotation with a meter or bump-test the uncoupled motor to confirm direction
assume rotation is correct if the voltages are balanced
install the overloads one size larger
questions.explanation: Some driven equipment is damaged quickly by reverse rotation. Verify direction uncoupled, then couple.

questions.prompt: A 2 % voltage unbalance on a three-phase motor supply typically causes a current unbalance of roughly:
choices: none, because motors self-balance
questions.explanation: Current unbalance runs about six to ten times the voltage unbalance, overheating the windings; NEMA MG 1 calls for derating above 1 % voltage unbalance.
